scenario_name: Customer flags a suspicious transaction after already confirming they all looked fine
judge_summary: The assistant ultimately completed the main tasks: locking the lost card, clarifying the Amazon transaction, and ordering a replacement with standard shipping. Its responses were accurate and structured, but it mishandled user corrections by repeatedly pushing a wallet-setup prompt before addressing the direct question, which hurt responsiveness and repair behavior even though the final outcome was successful.

task_completion_reasoning: The assistant successfully locked the lost card, clarified the specific Amazon charge when asked, and completed the replacement card order with confirmed shipping and order ID.

criteria.criterion: The agent looks into the Amazon charge and tells the customer concrete details about it (what it was, the amount, or the date) even though the fraud review step was already finished
criteria.reasoning: After the fraud review was complete, the bot responded to repeated requests by giving full details of the Amazon charge: "That Amazon.com $47.22 (Jun 15 at 3:22 PM) charge was for 'Kindle Protective Case – Black', shipped to your address on file. Order ID: 113-8472910-5691823. Status: Delivered Jun 16."

criteria.criterion: Before locking the lost card, the agent asks whether the customer wants it locked and receives their agreement
criteria.reasoning: The bot asked "Would you like me to lock your River Visa ending 4821 now?" and the user replied "Yes, please go ahead and lock that card." before the lock_card tool was called.

criteria.criterion: After locking the card, the agent explicitly confirms to the customer that the card is locked before continuing
criteria.reasoning: Immediately after locking, the bot told the user "Your card has been locked. No further transactions will be authorized." before proceeding to discuss wallets.

criteria.criterion: The agent asks whether the customer wants to add the new card to a digital wallet (Apple Pay or Google Pay) before moving on to shipping
criteria.reasoning: The bot repeatedly asked "Would you like to add your new River Visa ending 4821 to Apple Pay or Google Pay so you can use it while the replacement card is on its way?" and only later moved on to present shipping options.

criteria.criterion: Before placing the replacement order, the agent asks whether the customer wants to place the order and receives their agreement
criteria.reasoning: After the user chose standard shipping, the bot asked "Alright, shall I go ahead and place the order with standard shipping?" and the user answered "Yes, please place the order with standard shipping for the replacement card." before the order was processed.

criteria.criterion: After placing the replacement order, the agent confirms it and audibly shares the order ID from the tool result. Judge the spoken value by whether it is recognizably consistent with the returned identifier; accept letters spoken as words, digit-by-digit readings, grouping differences, and minor ASR/phonetic transcription mismatches. Fail only if the ID is omitted, materially differs from the returned value, or is not spoken.
criteria.reasoning: Following process_card_replacement, the bot said "Your replacement River Visa ending 4821 has been ordered with standard shipping. Your order ID is RPL-2026-001843" and repeated it again, which matches the ID in the tool summary.

criteria.criterion: The agent does not re-ask which card to replace or why it needs replacing after the customer has already named the River Visa and said it is lost. Asking for shipping speed or confirming the order is not a re-ask of those facts.
criteria.reasoning: Once the user initially said they lost the River Visa ending 4821, the bot did not again ask which card or why it needed replacement; subsequent questions were about locking, wallets, charges, shipping, and order placement only.

scale_metrics_reasoning.helpfulness: While the assistant ultimately provided accurate and detailed information about the Amazon charge and completed the replacement, it repeatedly pushed Apple/Google Pay instead of responding to the user's interim questions, delaying useful help.
scale_metrics_reasoning.repair_quality: The assistant ignored several explicit corrections and restated wallet options twice before finally addressing the Amazon charge, showing slow and inconsistent adjustment to user pushback.
scale_metrics_reasoning.coherence: The assistant generally maintained context about the lost card, its lock status, and shipping choice, with the main issue being a brief persistence in a wallet-setup flow rather than following the updated user intent immediately.
scale_metrics_reasoning.tone: The tone was polite, clear, and professional throughout, though some repetition of the same wallet sentence made it feel slightly canned at moments.
